title: Meet Python

cells.text: Welcome! This is a **notebook**, the same tool data analysts use every day. Each grey box is a **cell** that holds Python code. To **run** a cell, press its **Run** button (or Shift+Enter). The result appears right underneath.

cells.prompt: Press Run to run your first line of Python.

cells.text: `print()` shows whatever is inside its brackets. **Text** must go inside quotes, like `"Hello"`. **Numbers** don't need quotes, and Python can do maths with them: `+` is plus, `-` is minus, `*` is times, and `/` is divided by.

cells.prompt: Press Run. Python works out the maths first, then prints the answer.
Remember, * means times. What will this print? Pick one, then press Run.
This time the maths is inside quotes. What will it print? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: Quotes turn anything into text, so Python prints it exactly as typed and doesn't do the maths. Keep quotes for words, and leave them off for maths.

cells.prompt: Replace ___ with the sentence "I am learning Python", including the quotes, then press Run.
hints: Keep the quotes, because they tell Python it's text. Check the capital I and P.

cells.prompt: Your turn: make Python work out 12 + 30 and print the answer. Type the maths inside the brackets, without quotes, then press Run.
hints: No quotes this time, so Python does the maths.

recap: You ran your first Python! print() shows a result. Text goes in quotes, and maths goes without quotes.
